ad: Start: Aarey Milk Colony main gate, Goregaon East, Mumbai 400065
d: Quiet, green roads through Aarey Milk Colony with a steep climb - long-run and endurance territory for western-suburb runners, with almost no traffic in the early morning.
b: Distance runners, Hill training, Running groups

ad: Aksa Beach, Aksa Village, Malad West, Mumbai 400095
d: A roughly 3 km sandy beach lined with casuarina trees, one of the cleaner beaches in the city and a favourite for local morning walks and yoga. Do not swim - strong undertow, no lifeguards.
t: Best 6 AM – 7 PM (not recommended at night)

ad: Bandstand Promenade, Byramji Jeejeebhoy Rd, Bandra West, Mumbai 400050
d: A 1.2 km BMC-run sea walkway with a jogging track along the rocks, ending near Bandra Fort. Best early, before the sunset crowd.

ad: Bhakti Park, behind IMAX theatre, Wadala East, Mumbai 400037
d: A 25-acre park of grassland and wooded patches with over 4 km of jogging tracks and walking paths. Free and dog-friendly.

ad: Start: Carter Road promenade (north end), Bandra West, Mumbai 400050
d: A flat, tree-lined 1.25-1.5 km seafront path ending at Joggers Park, which can be extended through Chuim village to the Bandstand promenade for about 3.7 km one-way. Busy, so go early.

ad: Swatantrya Sainik Udyan (Chimni Garden), Borla, Union Park, Chembur East, Mumbai 400071
d: A quieter garden next to the golf course with a walking track and outdoor gym equipment.

ad: Chintamani Garden, Mulund East, Mumbai 400081
d: A small Mulund East garden with a short, flat walking loop of about 0.2 miles.

n: Coastal Road Promenade (Breach Candy to Worli)
ad: Start: Priyadarshini Park end, Nepean Sea Road / Breach Candy, Mumbai 400026
d: The new sea-facing promenade along the Mumbai Coastal Road: about 5.25 km currently open from Priyadarshini Park past Haji Ali to Worli, with separate walking paths and a cycling track. Free, wide and uninterrupted - now one of the longest continuous seafront runs in the city.
t: Promenade open 24 hours; gardens along it 8 AM – 8 PM

ad: Dadar Chowpatty, Dadar West, Mumbai 400028
d: A shoreline beach locals use for jogging and yoga, with a big view of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link at sunrise and sunset.

ad: Diamond Garden, VN Purav Marg (Sion-Trombay Road), Chembur East, Mumbai 400071
d: Chembur's best-known garden, with jogging and walking tracks, an open-air gym and a retired Gnat fighter jet by the entrance.

ad: DK Sandu Udyan, next to Joy Hospital, Chembur East, Mumbai 400071
d: A neighbourhood garden with a walking track, gazebo and shaded seating - an easy morning walk loop.

ad: Five Gardens, Dadar Parsi Colony, Matunga, Mumbai 400014
d: Five small gardens in the old Parsi colony between King's Circle and Dadar, joined by tree-shaded residential roads. Easy to stitch together a flat 3-4 km loop.

ad: Gandhi Maidan, Plot No. 155, D. Saraswati Marg, Mahadeo Wadi, Chembur East, Mumbai 400071
d: An open ground that hosts local running groups and sports training, including YMCA programmes.

ad: Girgaon Chowpatty, Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose Road, Girgaon, Mumbai 400007
d: The beach at the north end of Marine Drive, quiet in the early morning with locals walking, jogging and doing yoga on the sand. Easy to combine with a Marine Drive run.

n: Hanging Gardens and Kamala Nehru Park
ad: Hanging Gardens (Pherozeshah Mehta Gardens), Ridge Road, Malabar Hill, Mumbai 400006
d: Terraced gardens on top of Malabar Hill and the park opposite, popular with local morning walkers; an easy loop of about a mile with sea views.

ad: Jewel of Navi Mumbai, Sector 26, Nerul, Navi Mumbai
d: Landscaped lakeside park in Sector 26 Nerul with an open-air gym and a Yulu bike zone; a calm spot for an evening jog or walk close to Palm Beach Road.

ad: Jijamata Udyaan, Lalbaug Flyover, near Byculla, Byculla East, Mumbai 400027
d: The city's old botanical garden and zoo, with well-shaded paths and flowering trees - a calm daytime walking loop in central Mumbai.

ad: Joggers Park, Carter Road (south end), Bandra West, Mumbai 400050
d: Seaside park at the south end of Carter Road with a 400 m loop: a mud strip for running plus two paved walking tracks. Opened in 1990 and still one of the city's busiest jogging spots.

ad: Juhu Beachfront Public Park, 15 Gandhigram Rd, Jukarwadi, Juhu, Mumbai 400049
d: A compact green park by Juhu beach with about 1 km of looped paths and tree-covered walkways - handy for a structured run before or after the sand.

ad: Start: Juhu Chowpatty, Juhu Tara Road, Juhu, Mumbai 400049
d: About 3 miles (around 5 km) of wide, flat sand from Juhu to Versova; firm underfoot at low tide and quiet in the early morning.

ad: Mahalaxmi Race Course, Keshavrao Khadye Marg, Mahalaxmi, Mumbai
d: A 2.2 km dirt loop around the horse-racing track, opened to runners in the morning and evening. The soft surface is easier on the joints than the seafronts, which is why marathon trainees like it.

ad: Maharashtra Nature Park, Sion Bandra Link Road, opp. Dharavi Bus Depot, Dharavi, Mumbai 400017
d: A 37-acre man-made forest on the Mithi river with shaded trails, including a ficus trail out to the Mahim creek mangroves. A walk rather than a run: go at opening for the birds and butterflies.

ad: Mahim Beach, Mahim Bay, near Mahim Fort / Mahim Koliwada, Mumbai 400016
d: A roughly 1 km beach on Mahim Bay with an emerging promenade, views across to Bandra and Worli, and early-morning joggers. Short and local rather than a long run.

ad: Elevated Nature Trail, Walkeshwar, Malabar Hill, Mumbai 400006
d: A raised wooden walkway through the treetops of Malabar Hill's forest, with views out over the city and sea. A slow walk rather than a run.

ad: Mango Garden, CBD Belapur, Navi Mumbai
d: Small neighbourhood garden in Belapur, good for a short walk or easy laps with kids.

ad: Start: Marine Drive near Wilson College, Girgaon Chowpatty, Mumbai 400007
d: Mumbai's classic seafront run: about 4.3 km of flat promenade from Wilson College to Nariman Point, with the sea on one side and the skyline on the other. Well lit, so it works at night too, though it gets crowded even early.

ad: Millennium Garden, Ghatkopar East, Mumbai
d: A free, central Ghatkopar East garden with walking paths and benches.

ad: Mindspace Garden, MDP Road, Mindspace, Malad West, Mumbai 400064
d: A BMC-run garden in the Mindspace business district with over a hundred tree species, gazebos, a joggers' path and steps that double as a cardio workout. Free.

ad: Start: lake entrance off Palm Beach Road, Nerul, Navi Mumbai
d: A dedicated 2.7 km path around Nerul Lake, also called Seawoods lake, just off Palm Beach Road. Traffic-free and pleasant for easy loops or a cool-down after the road run.

ad: Nirvana Park, Hiranandani Gardens, Powai, Mumbai 400076
d: A 4-acre landscaped park with a lit stone running track around lawns, a pond, gazebos and little bridges.

ad: Oval Maidan, between Maharishi Karve Road and the Bombay High Court, Fort, Mumbai 400032
d: A 22-acre heritage maidan with a jogging track around its edge, framed by Victorian Gothic and Art Deco buildings. No gates or fees; quieter on weekday mornings than on Sundays, when the cricket takes over.

ad: Start: Ahilya Gokul Patil Rd junction, Palm Beach Road, Nerul, Navi Mumbai
d: The 10 km six-lane road from Vashi to Belapur along the harbour is Navi Mumbai's favourite long run: smooth and well kept, with a footpath or shoulder for much of it. Go early, before the traffic builds.

n: Powai Lake promenade and Hiranandani Garden
ad: Start: Hiranandani Garden, Hiranandani Gardens, Powai, Mumbai 400076
d: A 5.5 km mixed route: garden paths at Hiranandani, a 1.4 km lakeside promenade along Powai Lake, then wooded trails in Forest Park. Go early morning or late afternoon.

ad: Priyadarshini Park, Nepean Sea Road, Malabar Hill, Mumbai 400006
d: A sea-facing 20-acre park with a 400 m synthetic track and a 500 m coconut-lined dirt path - the place in South Mumbai for laps and intervals away from traffic.

ad: Rajawadi Garden, Ghatkopar East, Mumbai 400077
d: A small neighbourhood garden in Ghatkopar East with a short, flat walking loop of about 0.2 miles - fine for an easy morning walk close to home.

n: Rajiv Gandhi Joggers Park & Mini Seashore
ad: Rajiv Gandhi Joggers Park, Sector 10A, Juhu Nagar, Vashi, Navi Mumbai
d: One of the best running spots in Navi Mumbai: a flat 2.5 km path around a pond in a dedicated park, away from traffic. A bridge links it to the Vashi Mini Seashore (Juhu Chowpatty).

ad: Rock Garden, Nerul, Navi Mumbai
d: One of Nerul's well-known gardens, a green stop for a short jog or walk.

ad: Sagar Vihar, Sector 6, Vashi, Navi Mumbai
d: Waterfront promenade in Sector 6 Vashi that's popular with morning and evening joggers; a bridge connects it to the Mini Seashore. Hawkers can crowd it in the evenings.

n: Sambhaji Park (Sambhaji Raje Maidan), Mulund East
ad: Sambhaji Park Version II, Deendayal Nagar, Mulund East, Mumbai 400081
d: A big sports ground with a jogging track of almost 700 m, lit at night, plus an open gym and courts - Mulund East's go-to loop.

n: SGNP main gate to Kanheri Caves
ad: Sanjay Gandhi National Park main gate, Western Express Highway, Borivali East, Mumbai 400066
d: A 6 km one-way climb on the park road from the main gate to the Kanheri Caves through forest, with deer and birds along the way. Medium difficulty; park entry fees apply.
b: Distance runners, Hill training, Nature lovers
t: Tue – Sun 7:30 AM – 6:30 PM (last entry 5 PM, closed Mon)

ad: Shivaji Park, Dadar West, Mumbai 400028 (pedestrian gate on the east side)
d: Mumbai's largest park (27 acres) with a flat 1.3 km perimeter path, the home ground of several running groups and marathon clubs. Easy to add laps or explore the interior paths.

ad: Veer Savarkar Udyan, Lokmanya Tilak Road, Gautam Nagar, Borivali West, Mumbai 400092
d: A seven-acre garden shaded by banyan and pipal trees, with a 1.5 km jogging track around its edge and a lake in the middle. About 10 minutes from Borivali station.

ad: Versova Beach, Versova, Andheri West, Mumbai 400061
d: A wide stretch of sand, less crowded than Juhu and much cleaner since the volunteer clean-up drives began in 2015 - good for a sunrise jog.

ad: Wonders Park, Sector 18, Nerul, Navi Mumbai
d: Big NMMC park in Sector 18 Nerul with replicas of the Seven Wonders, fountains and rides; paths suit easy jogs and family walks, and there's an NMMC open-air gym in the sector.

ad: Start: Worli Sea Face near Worli Post Office (Sea Link end), Khan Abdul Gaffar Khan Rd, Worli
d: A flat, roughly 2.75 km waterfront road with a 1.5 km separated path that starts just south of the Bandra-Worli Sea Link. Good for first-timers and interval work; go early, it gets windy and busy.

n: Aarey Colony: Goregaon East to Powai
ad: Start: Aarey Milk Colony, Goregaon East, Mumbai 400065
d: A roughly 9.6 km ride on quiet, tree-lined Aarey roads from Goregaon East to Powai, past lakes, gardens and the Chhota Kashmir area. Easy-moderate (2/5).

ad: Start: Priyadarshini Park end, Breach Candy, Mumbai 400026
d: A dedicated cycling track along the new Coastal Road promenade, with ramps at the underpasses, running about 5.25 km from Breach Candy past Haji Ali to Worli. Free and traffic-free.

ad: Start: Gorai Jetty, Borivali West, Mumbai 400091
d: Ferry across Gorai creek and ride the village roads, hills and beach of Gorai and Manori past the Global Vipassana Pagoda - an easy, roughly 22-30 km ride with a real out-of-city feel inside Mumbai.
t: Early morning (ferries from ~7 AM on organised rides)

n: Marine Drive to Fort and Colaba loop
ad: Start: Marine Drive, near Girgaon Chowpatty, Mumbai 400020
d: A flat, roughly 15 km city ride: 3.5 km of seafront on Marine Drive, then Nariman Point, Churchgate, the Fort precinct and Colaba. Ride early morning or late night to avoid traffic.
t: Best early morning or late night

n: Mulund to Yeoor Hills MTB trail
ad: Start: Mulund West, Mumbai 400080
d: A hard (5/5) mountain-bike ride of about 12.7 km from Mulund into the Yeoor hills, with dirt sections, woods, lakes and monsoon waterfalls. Skilled riders only; don't ride solo.

n: SGNP: main gate to Kanheri Caves
ad: Sanjay Gandhi National Park main gate, Western Express Highway, Borivali East, Mumbai 400066
d: Mumbai's best-known forest ride: about 7 km one way on the park road, flat at first and then a steady climb to the Kanheri Caves. Cycles can be rented at the park entrance.

n: Andheri Sports Complex Pool (Shahaji Raje Krida Sankul)
ad: Andheri Sports Complex, Veera Desai Road, Andheri West, Mumbai 400053
d: BMC's sports complex with an Olympic-size pool and a four-level diving pool - the western suburbs' main competition-grade pool.

ad: Chacha Nehru Ground, Malad West, Mumbai

ad: Worli Reservoir Hill, Worli, Mumbai
d: A BMC pool on Worli Reservoir Hill, listed among the city pools running BMC's 21-day summer swimming courses.

ad: YMCA Marg, Sector 8, CBD Belapur, Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra 400614
d: Swimming pool at the Bombay YMCA Navi Mumbai branch on YMCA Marg, CBD Belapur; the branch also has a gym and a basketball court.

d: A Bandra club with a year-round, temperature-controlled pool.

ad: Sharadbhau Acharya Marg, near Natraj Cinema, Chembur East, Mumbai 400071
d: BMC Olympic-size pool (50 m) with a separate kids' pool, run on annual membership booked through the BMC pool portal. One of the eastern suburbs' main lap-swimming options.

d: Long-running municipal pool in Ghatkopar East, one of BMC's original six city pools.

d: A competitive-swimming programme with largely subsidised coaching, including SAI-Glenmark scholarships for talented young swimmers.

ad: Mumbai
Khodkona village, Palghar district
d: A hard, roughly 3-hour trek to the largest fort in the Palghar region, with a rock-climbing section that is risky in the monsoon. Water available all year.

ad: Belapur Fort, Uran Road, Sector 32, Seawoods / CBD Belapur, Navi Mumbai
d: Ruins of a Siddi-built hilltop fort near the mouth of Panvel Creek, later held by the Portuguese, Marathas and British. A short heritage hike; the fort is in a dilapidated state.

ad: Khandas village, 34 km from Karjat, Raigad district
d: A long, hard forest trek of 6-7 hours up the Ganesh Ghat (or steeper Shidi Ghat) to the Bhimashankar temple plateau. Water all along.

ad: Chincholi village, between Badlapur and Vangani, Thane district
d: A hard trek to a 2,330 ft plateau fort visible from the Kalyan-Karjat train line; about 1.5 hours from Chincholi with rock-climbing moves near the top. Lovely waterfalls at the base in monsoon.

n: Conservation Education Centre (CEC) nature trails, Aarey
ad: Conservation Education Centre, Film City Complex, Aarey Milk Colony, Goregaon East, Mumbai 400065
d: A nature centre inside the forest at Film City with a butterfly park, birdwatching and guided weekend walks that follow leopard trails.

ad: Gilbert Hill, near Bhavan's College, Andheri West, Mumbai 400058
d: A 200 ft column of black basalt, about 66 million years old, climbed by rock-cut steps in five minutes or so. The Gaodevi-Durgamata temple on top looks out over Andheri to the sea and Aarey.

ad: Dehri village, Murbad, Thane district
d: A medium, roughly 2-hour climb from Dehri with a near-vertical rock-cut section, caves and a Mahadeo temple on top. Water all year.

ad: Harshewadi / Nirgudpada, near Trimbakeshwar, Nashik district
d: Famous for its near-vertical rock-cut steps carved with hand grooves. Medium grade: about 1 hour from Harshewadi or 2 hours from Nirgudpada; cisterns on top.

ad: Khireshwar village (or Pachnai), near Malshej Ghat, Ahmednagar district
d: A 4,000 ft plateau fort with ancient caves, the Kedareshwar cave temple and the famous Konkan Kada cliff. Medium grade, often done as an overnight trek.

ad: Bari village, Akole taluka, Ahmednagar district
d: The highest peak in Maharashtra at 5,400 ft. A medium, roughly 13 km round trip from Bari with ladders near the top; about 3 hours up and 5-6 hours return. No water on the route - fill up in Bari.

ad: Karnala Bird Sanctuary, Mumbai-Goa Highway, near Panvel, Raigad
d: An easy trek through Karnala Bird Sanctuary to a fort topped by a 125 ft basalt pillar (Pandu's tower). About 1.5 hours up; the forest trail is roughly 2.7 km with rest stops.

ad: Vaghote village, Wada-Palghar road, Palghar district
d: A medium, roughly 2-hour climb from Vaghote to a plateau with cisterns, a Shiva temple and a human-shaped rock pinnacle.

ad: Peth Shahapur village, near Aamby Valley road, Lonavala, Pune district
d: One of the easiest fort treks near Mumbai - about 30 minutes from Peth Shahapur - with largely intact walls you can walk around.

ad: Peth village via Ambivali, about 30 km from Karjat, Raigad district
d: A medium climb to a fort with a rock-cut internal staircase in its pinnacle; about an hour up from Peth village. Reliable cistern near the cave.

ad: Lohagadwadi / Malavli, Maval, Pune district
d: An easy, popular fort trek near Lonavala, about 3,400 ft high, with drinking water all year and the Bhaja caves on the way. Connected to Visapur by a ridge.

ad: Mahuli village, via Asangaon station, Shahapur, Thane district
d: A cluster of three peaks; the main Mahuli summit is about 2 hours from the Asangaon side. Water in cisterns by the gatehouses.

ad: Haji Malang base, about 16 km south of Kalyan, Thane district
d: A medium 3,200 ft fort above the Haji Malang dargah; about 2 hours from the base, with a vertical rock face near the top. Water tanks on the fort.

ad: Vadgaon village, near Patalganga MIDC, Raigad district
d: A medium, roughly 3-hour forest climb near Patalganga; no facilities on top so carry food.

ad: Naneghat base (Vaishakhare side), via Murbad, Thane district
d: An easy trek up an ancient Satavahana trade pass to rock-cut caves with Brahmi inscriptions and the thumb-shaped 'Nana's Thumb' peak.

ad: Parsik Hill Road, off Sector 30, CBD Belapur, Navi Mumbai
d: Hilltop on the CBD Belapur side of Parsik Hill, used for morning and evening walks with views over Navi Mumbai; the hill is historically a hiking and rock-climbing spot. Often closed in the rains because of landslides.

ad: Near Neral station, Raigad district
d: A medium, roughly 3-hour climb from Neral through dense forest to caves, a temple and views of Matheran, Chanderi and Prabalgad. Called one of the most beautiful one-day treks.

ad: Thakurwadi, via Shedung junction, Old Panvel-Pune Highway, Raigad
d: A medium trek to Prabalmachi plateau and its two forts: Prabalgad, and the steep rock-cut steps of the Kalavantin pinnacle (about 45 minutes up from the col). Water available all year.

ad: Udhewadi village, Rajmachi, Maval, Pune district
d: Twin forts (Shrivardhan and Manaranjan) above a hamlet on a plateau. Medium: about 4 hours from Kondivade (Karjat side) or a 19 km, 5-hour walk from Lonavala via Tungarli. Water available in the village.

ad: Ratanwadi village, Bhandardara, Ahmednagar district
d: A medium, roughly 2-hour climb up ladders or rock-cut steps to a fort with a natural rock window ('Nedhe') and views over Bhandardara.

ad: Starts at Kanheri Caves, Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Borivali East, Mumbai 400066
d: A medium, 3-4 hour guided trail from Kanheri Caves up to around 1,000 ft - one of the park's best birding routes, with a waterfall crossing in season.

ad: Sanjay Gandhi National Park main gate, Western Express Highway, Borivali East, Mumbai 400066
d: Walk, cycle or ride up to a 2,000-year-old complex of more than 100 Buddhist rock-cut caves inside the park. The lower trail is easy, around 5-6 km from near the entrance.
t: Caves 9 AM – 12:30 PM, 2 – 5:30 PM (per guide); park closed Mon

ad: Sanjay Gandhi National Park, Borivali East, Mumbai 400066 (trail 4-5 km from the main gate)
d: An easy guided trail along the park's western edge through dry-deciduous to evergreen forest.

ad: Nagla Block, Sasupada, off Ghodbunder Road / Mumbai-Ahmedabad highway, Thane district
d: An easy 3 km guided forest trail in SGNP's northern Nagla block, about 2-2.5 hours.

ad: Sanjay Gandhi National Park, near the Toy Train junction bus parking (~500 m from main gate), Borivali East, Mumbai 400066
d: A guided forest walk of about 2 km to the first stream (around 2 hours), with permission to go on to more streams and a waterfall. Needs a forest permit and escort, booked through the park's Nature Information Centre or a walk organiser.

ad: Sondewadi village, near Karjat, Raigad district
d: A short, lesser-known trek near Karjat with a ladder over the final 15 ft rock patch and good mountain views. About 2 hours from Sondewadi.

ad: Pachhapur village, near Pali, Raigad district
d: An easy, roughly 2-hour climb to a huge fort often called a replica of Raigad, with plenty of water tanks and space to stay overnight.

ad: Tandulwadi village, about 4.5 km from Saphale Road station, Palghar district
d: A medium, roughly 2-hour climb from Tandulwadi village with the Vaitarna river below - one of the few fort treks reachable straight from the Western line.

ad: Tikona Peth village, Pawna Maval, Pune district
d: An easy, compact triangular fort - about an hour up from Tikona Peth - with views of Lohagad, Visapur, Tung and Pawna lake. Potable water all year.

ad: Tungwadi village, Pawna, Pune district
d: A short, steep cone above Pawna lake; about 45 minutes to the top. Easy enough for a half-day add-on to a Lonavala trip.
